title: TNK1 is a targetable JAK-independent driver of STAT signaling and inflammation.
authors: Lopez-Palacios, Tania P; Madhusanka, Deshan; Scott, Samuel M; Vaughan, Alec J; Egbert, Christina M; Chan, Tsz-Yin; Bustos, Yaphet; Ashworth, Spencer W; Truman, Jacob M; Per Moreno, Angela; Tsang, Tsz-Ming; Jayatunge, Dasun N; Yang, Jingshu; Nelson, Paige; Al-Sudani, Fatima; Tarara, Madelyn; Kohler, Emmalee; Pereira Mendiola, Nelson E; Soderblom, Erik J; Stubben, Chris J; Stewart, Paul A; Kolasangiani, Reza; Dobish, Kasidy K; Knobel, Beate; Buckley, Shannon M; Bidone, Tamara C; Smoot, Rory L; Uchida, Amiko M; Morawe, Mareen; Armacki, Milena; Andersen, Joshua L
one_liner_zh: 该文研究TNK1激酶通过非JAK途径磷酸化STAT1转录因子并驱动炎症，虽涉及STAT1转录因子但核心是激酶-底物磷酸化与凝聚体调控，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Deregulated inflammatory signaling via STAT family transcription factors, particularly STAT1, underlies a variety of immune-related diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease. Whereas activation of STATs by JAKs via canonical receptor-driven JAK-STAT signaling is well understood, little is known about JAK-independent mechanisms of STAT activation. Here, we identify the understudied nonreceptor tyrosine kinase TNK1 as a therapeutically targetable, JAK-independent activator of STAT signaling. Using a multiomics approach, we mapped a network of TNK1 substrates associated with protein condensates and proinflammatory signaling, including STAT1. We found that TNK1, but not its sister kinase ACK1, directly phosphorylates STATs at well described STAT-activating JAK sites. In cells, TNK1-mediated STAT1 phosphorylation and activation occurs independently of JAKs. Imaging and interactomics data suggest that TNK1 interacts with STAT1 in cytosolic condensates, which likely compartmentalize TNK1-substrate interactions. We show that an intrinsically disordered proline-rich region in TNK1, which includes a 14-3-3 docking phosphorylation site, is required for the formation of kinase-active TNK1 condensates and STAT1 phosphorylation. Mutations within the proline-rich region that eliminate 14-3-3 binding increase formation of TNK1 condensates, suggesting a model in which 14-3-3 acts as a clamp that constrains the flexible PRR to inhibit condensate formation and STAT1 activation. Finally, we show that TNK1 is a targetable driver of STAT1-mediated inflammation in the gut as inhibition of TNK1 reduces active STAT1 in the colon and ameliorates colitis symptoms in mice.
abstract_zh: 通过STAT家族转录因子（尤其是STAT1）介导的炎症信号失调，是多种免疫相关疾病（包括炎症性肠病）的基础。尽管JAK通过经典的受体驱动的JAK-STAT信号通路激活STATs已被充分理解，但关于JAK非依赖性STAT激活机制知之甚少。在此，我们识别出研究不足的非受体酪氨酸激酶TNK1作为可治疗靶向的、JAK非依赖性的STAT信号激活因子。利用多组学方法，我们绘制了与蛋白凝聚体和促炎信号（包括STAT1）相关的TNK1底物网络。我们发现，TNK1（而非其姊妹激酶ACK1）在已充分描述的STAT激活JAK位点直接磷酸化STATs。在细胞中，TNK1介导的STAT1磷酸化和激活独立于JAK发生。成像和相互作用组学数据表明，TNK1在胞质凝聚体中与STAT1相互作用，这可能将TNK1-底物相互作用区室化。我们证明，TNK1中一个内在无序的富含脯氨酸区域（包括一个14-3-3对接磷酸化位点）是形成激酶活性TNK1凝聚体和STAT1磷酸化所必需的。富含脯氨酸区域内消除14-3-3结合的突变增加了TNK1凝聚体的形成，提示一个模型，其中14-3-3作为钳制物约束柔性PRR以抑制凝聚体形成和STAT1激活。最后，我们证明TNK1是肠道中STAT1介导炎症的可靶向驱动因子，因为抑制TNK1可减少小鼠结肠中的活性STAT1并改善结肠炎症状。
